binds: BY READING. No code consumer, no gate (PRD s.5 'Any gate' stands; Andrew has not asked for one). What reads it today: (1) the `answer_state` block of every per-tool result deliverable at org/missions/D11/NFRA/NFRA_COMPEFFICACY/deliverables/<serial>/<tool>.result.md -- its KEYS are exactly the four `state` values below; (2) the certifier's 4.3 grade -- a key outside the four is a non-conforming deliverable, returned not graded (PRD s.4 'every field is REQUIRED'). T-16 (comp-adversary.result.md @d101d4fe20) already conforms: 4 of 4 keys match.

grain.what_one_member_classifies: ONE RUN's answer about ONE subject when that answer is not a plain positive result. Never a tool (a tool is CLEARED/RETIRED/DOES-NOT-EXIST/CARRIED -- PRD s.2, a different axis), never a project, never a preflight.
grain.two_grains_kept_apart: STATE = the spelling, the grading key (exactly one per state). TOOL-VOICE = the token an ENGINE prints in its own output when it names the state itself; adopted from a live carrier where one exists, otherwise null. PRD s.4.7's census line 'NOT_DECIDABLE -> NOT-DECIDABLE' mixed the two grains: it named comp-schedule's printed token as if it were a state. s.4.3 has no fifth state; the token belongs to PARTIAL_OR_BLIND.
grain.normalize: exact -- a consumer compares bytes; it does NOT fold case or separators (folding would make 'one spelling' meaningless).

states.meaning: the subject does not exist where the tool looks (PRD s.4.3). SUBJECT = the thing the tool was pointed at (a path, an artifact, a pathspec/scope), NOT the pattern searched for.

kin_not_a_spelling: comp-find's denominator shape '0 hit(s) across 0 file(s)' -- ZERO FILES scanned = the pathspec is not in the corpus. CLAUDE.md Rule 21 names that shape 'OUT-OF-CORPUS, NOT ABSENCE': Rule 21's 'absence' means the PATTERN is absent (that is PRESENT_WITH_ZERO_RESULTS); this state is the SCOPE being absent. Same shape, this state.

'OUT-OF-CORPUS' is PROSE, not a printed token: comp-read --enumerate 'OUT[-_]OF[-_]CORPUS' over .tools/comp-find (615 lines) = 0 hits; census corpus=all 111 hits / 145,918 files, SURFACED=3 CONFIG=2 DOC=106, the only first-party code hit a COMMENT at .tools/_comprail.py:382. losing_carrier.why_it_loses_without_changing: Rule 24 postulate (iii), intent coherence: DECLARED-NOT-APPLICABLE is declared by a PERSON about whether to RUN a lens; NOT_APPLICABLE is measured by a RUN about its SUBJECT. Under this enum the two tokens never compete for one field.

not_applicable_split_finding.residual_declared_not_hidden: the four state spellings use the underscore separator; the one adopted tool-voice token that differs from its state (NOT-DECIDABLE) uses a hyphen because that is what the live carrier prints and a live carrier is adopted, never re-minted. A consumer compares exact bytes per grain (state keys against `state`; a tool's printed token against `tool_voice.token`); it never folds separators.

rule_24_record.i_MECE_over_a_declared_domain: DOMAIN: one RUN's answer about one subject when it is not a plain positive result. Four members, decided by three questions in order: does the subject exist where the tool looks? (no -> SUBJECT_ABSENT_FROM_CORPUS) / is the question well-formed for this subject-tool pair? (no -> NOT_APPLICABLE) / did the tool examine the whole space it claims? (no -> PARTIAL_OR_BLIND; yes and zero -> PRESENT_WITH_ZERO_RESULTS). UNCOVERED-MEMBER HUNT: a plain positive result (hits > 0, complete) is outside the domain by construction -- the answer IS the result; a run that prints NOTHING (crash, KILLED-OUTSIDE by the harness) has NO state -- this enum classifies what a tool SAYS, and saying nothing is precisely the AC-2 failure it exists to make rejectable, not a fifth member. EXCLUSIVITY exercised: T-16 planted one case per state and got four distinguishable outputs; the one overlap candidate found (comp-schedule's NOT-DECIDABLE: blind vs not-applicable) is resolved by question 2 -- the question applies.
rule_24_record.ii_same_grain: every member classifies ONE RUN's answer (never a tool's disposition, never a project's stage, never a preflight lens). The state spelling and the tool-voice token are two grains and sit in two fields; s.4.7's census collapsed them and that collapse produced the phantom 'NOT_DECIDABLE' state.
rule_24_record.iii_intent_coherence: one intent: 'why is this answer not a plain positive result', from the run's point of view. Excluded on intent: DECLARED-NOT-APPLICABLE (an author's preflight declaration -- see the finding); CLEARED/RETIRED/DOES-NOT-EXIST/CARRIED (a tool's disposition, PRD s.2/s.7); DONE/IN-FLIGHT/OPEN/HELD/NOT-EVALUATED (a decomp cell's status).
rule_24_record.iv_state_coherence: which values one remedy does NOT move: a coverage/corpus fix moves PARTIAL_OR_BLIND toward a positive result or PRESENT_WITH_ZERO_RESULTS; it does NOT move NOT_APPLICABLE (a correct result) and does NOT move SUBJECT_ABSENT_FROM_CORPUS (the subject is what it is). A 'say it in your own voice' remedy (T-16 F1 class) moves a tool from crashing/silent to printing the tool-voice token; it moves NO state. This ratification moves the spellings from by-reading to data; it moves NO tool's output.

reading_check.what: the check a reader runs to reject a malformed copy of THIS file -- stdlib, one line (build ladder rung 6). It is the consumer this file names for its negative control; it is NOT a gate and is not wired to any hook.
reading_check.python_c: import json,sys;p=sys.argv[1];d=json.load(open(p));s=d['states'];n=lambda x:x.upper().replace('-','_');assert len(s)==4,'REJECT: %d states -- the enum has exactly four'%len(s);assert len({x['state'] for x in s})==4,'REJECT: duplicate state';assert len({n(x['state']) for x in s})==4,'REJECT: a second spelling of an existing state';t=[x['tool_voice']['token'] for x in s if x['tool_voice']['token']];assert len(t)==len(set(t)),'REJECT: tool-voice token reused across states';print('OK: 4 states, one spelling each; tool-voice tokens',t)

a tool-voice token reused across two states
